title: Creating POST, PUT, and PATCH Routes
summary: Builds the three write endpoints of the joke API in the DIY project: POST /jokes to add a joke, PUT /jokes/:id to replace one completely, and PATCH /jokes/:id to change only the supplied fields. Each is a challenge followed by a walkthrough.

concepts.heading: Challenge 4: POST /jokes (create)
points: The client sends the new joke in the request body as x-www-form-urlencoded data with two fields, text and type (set these in Postman's Body tab).

The id is not supplied by the client. It is generated as jokes.length + 1, so with 100 jokes the next id is 101, then 102 and so on. (Extra) This breaks if jokes are ever deleted, since lengths and ids drift apart; using the highest existing id plus one is safer.

The starter file already registers body-parser (bodyParser.urlencoded with extended: true) via app.use, which is the middleware that fills req.body. Express has its own built-in parser, but body-parser is kept for clarity and because it is widely used.
Build a newJoke object with id, jokeText (from req.body.text) and jokeType (from req.body.type), then jokes.push(newJoke) to add it to the end of the array.
console.log(jokes.slice(-1)) prints the last array element: a negative index to slice counts from the end, and the result is a one-item array.
Respond with res.json(newJoke) so the client can confirm what was created. The response comes from the object built out of the request, not from re-reading the array; that is a design choice.
Possible extensions mentioned: validate text length and restrict type to an allowed list. They are not required.

concepts.heading: Challenge 5: PUT /jokes/:id (full replacement)
points: PUT means a complete update: every non-automatic field must be sent, and the stored resource is overwritten with them. The id stays the same because it identifies the item.
Because the whole object is replaced, a field sent blank or left out ends up empty in the stored joke. That is correct PUT behaviour.
In Postman the id goes in the path (Params > Path Variables, e.g. 2) and text and type go in the form-encoded body.

Handler steps: read the id from req.params.id (parseInt for strict comparison, or use ==), build replacementJoke = { id, jokeText: req.body.text, jokeType: req.body.type }, locate the position with findIndex, assign jokes[searchIndex] = replacementJoke, then respond with the new object.
Array.prototype.findIndex(callback) is like find, but returns the index of the first match (or -1 if none), which is what is needed to overwrite an element in place.
A real API would normally implement either PUT or PATCH for updates; both are shown here for practice.

concepts.heading: Challenge 6: PATCH /jokes/:id (partial update)
points: PATCH changes only part of a resource and is what most updates really need (e.g. change one field of a user without resending everything).
The example goal: change the type of joke 2 to a new category such as Agriculture while leaving its text alone.

Handler steps: parseInt the id, find the existing joke, then build replacementJoke with each field set to req.body.field || existingJoke.field. The || operator keeps the value from the request when it is present (truthy) and otherwise falls back to the stored value.
Then findIndex on the same id, overwrite jokes[searchIndex] with replacementJoke, and send it back as JSON.
The same logic could be written with if statements for readability; the || form is a common compact idiom. Test it in a console if it is unfamiliar.
(Extra) The || fallback cannot set a field to an empty string or other falsy value; ?? or an explicit undefined check handles that.

concepts.heading: Verifying
points: Run index.js with nodemon and send the POST, PUT and PATCH requests from the JokeAPI collection (check both the Params and Body tabs, which are pre-filled). Before the routes exist Postman shows an error; once they work it shows the expected JSON.
Re-read any unfamiliar method (slice, find, findIndex) on MDN before moving on.

task.name: DIY API: POST, PUT and PATCH routes
task.starting_point: The DIY API project from the previous lecture with the three GET routes done; index.js has empty slots for challenges 4-6 and body-parser already configured; the JokeAPI Postman collection has the POST, PUT and PATCH requests ready.
task.goal: Implement POST /jokes, PUT /jokes/:id and PATCH /jokes/:id so the Postman requests succeed and the in-memory jokes array changes accordingly.
steps: Challenge 4: add app.post('/jokes', ...) that builds newJoke with id jokes.length + 1 and text/type from req.body, pushes it onto jokes, logs the last item and responds with the new joke.

Challenge 5: add app.put('/jokes/:id', ...) that parses the id, builds a replacement object from the id and body fields, uses findIndex to locate the joke, overwrites that slot and responds with the replacement.
Challenge 6: add app.patch('/jokes/:id', ...) that finds the existing joke and builds a replacement using req.body.x || existing.x for text and type, writes it back by index and responds with it.
Run nodemon index.js and send the POST, PUT and PATCH requests from the Postman collection, checking Params and Body.
Re-send a GET for the changed id (or filter by type) to confirm the data actually changed.
task.expected_result: POST returns the new joke with the next id; PUT with id 2 returns joke 2 fully replaced (blank fields become empty); PATCH with only type=Agriculture returns joke 2 with the new type and original text.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 30 - Build Your Own API/30.02 DIY API/solution.js

pitfalls: Sending the body as JSON or raw in Postman when the server only has the urlencoded parser, leaving req.body fields undefined; use x-www-form-urlencoded.
Forgetting parseInt on the id, so === never finds a match and findIndex returns -1 (writing jokes[-1] silently adds a bogus property).
(Extra) PATCH on an unknown id: existingJoke is undefined and reading its properties throws; no 404 handling is shown.
Mistaking PUT for a partial update; omitted fields are wiped.
(Extra) Data lives only in memory, so restarts (nodemon reloads) reset all additions and edits.

gaps_and_ideas: New lesson 'Write routes: POST, PUT, PATCH' with a blurb contrasting create, replace and amend.

Tasks: (1) POST a new item with an auto id, (2) PUT to replace an item by id, (3) PATCH with the || fallback, (4) (Extra) PATCH using ?? so empty strings can be saved, (5) (Extra) return 404 JSON when the id is not found.
Starter code idea: Express server with body-parser and a short array, route stubs marked TODO.
